units.title: Foundations for Advanced Java: Threads, I/O and Serialization
topics: The map of the Java platform
Collections and generics in a line
Seeing the ideas: threads, streams and serialization

sections.title: The map of the Java platform
Collections and generics in a line
Seeing the ideas: threads, streams and serialization

summary: A thread is an independent path of execution sharing the process's memory; shared mutable data needs synchronisation.
Executors and futures are the practical way to run tasks concurrently and collect results.
Java I/O is layered streams; try-with-resources and java.nio.file make file work short and safe.
Serialization turns an object graph into bytes (and back) and underlies persistence and RMI; transient fields are not saved.

units.title: GUI Programming: Swing, Layouts and Event Handling
topics: Seeing the ideas: windows, layouts, events and MVC

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: windows, layouts, events and MVC

summary: Swing components (J...) form a tree under a top-level container and are drawn by the event dispatch thread; long work belongs in a SwingWorker.
Layout managers position components; nesting panels with different managers builds any layout.
In the delegation event model a source notifies registered listeners; adapters and lambdas shorten the code.
Swing separates models from views (MVC): changing the model updates every view through events.
JavaFX offers a scene graph, binding, CSS and FXML as a modern alternative.

units.title: Database Programming with JDBC
topics: SQL injection and why we use PreparedStatement
The DAO pattern and connection pools
Seeing the ideas: drivers, cursors, transactions and pools

sections.title: SQL injection and why we use PreparedStatement
The DAO pattern and connection pools
Seeing the ideas: drivers, cursors, transactions and pools

summary: JDBC defines database-independent interfaces; a vendor driver (type 4 today) implements them; the program loads the driver, connects, runs SQL and processes results.
PreparedStatement is faster for repeated SQL and the cure for SQL injection; ResultSet is a cursor and metadata describes its columns.
Transactions make groups of statements atomic through commit and rollback; batching reduces round trips.
RowSets offer disconnected, scrollable data; the DAO pattern and connection pools separate persistence from the rest of the application.

units.title: Network Programming with Sockets and HTTP
topics: Seeing the ideas: addresses, sockets, datagrams and HTTP

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: addresses, sockets, datagrams and HTTP

summary: A TCP socket is a reliable byte-stream connection; the server accepts connections and typically serves each in its own thread; the client connects, writes and reads.
UDP sockets send independent packets without a connection or guarantees.
The JDK includes an HTTP client and a small HTTP server; URI/URL split names into their parts.
Real programs need timeouts, framing, TLS, validation and cleanup.

units.title: Remote Method Invocation and CORBA
topics: Parameters: by value or by reference
Seeing the ideas: stubs, copies, wire bytes and failures

sections.title: Parameters: by value or by reference
Seeing the ideas: stubs, copies, wire bytes and failures

summary: RMI lets a client call methods on an object in another JVM through a stub; a registry maps names to stubs; the transport is TCP (JRMP).
Serializable arguments are copied (so the server cannot change the caller's object), remote objects are referenced; the object's state stays on the server.
Distribution adds failure modes, so remote methods declare RemoteException and callers must handle partial failure.
CORBA offers language-neutral distributed objects with IDL, an ORB and IIOP but is obsolete in the JDK; REST and gRPC are today's choices.

units.title: Servlets and JavaServer Pages
topics: GET and POST, forms and parameters
Filters, listeners and the request dispatcher
The MVC pattern with servlets and JSP
Seeing the ideas: containers, sessions, filters and JSP

sections.title: GET and POST, forms and parameters
Filters, listeners and the request dispatcher
The MVC pattern with servlets and JSP
Seeing the ideas: containers, sessions, filters and JSP

summary: A servlet container runs Java servlets that turn HTTP requests into responses; one instance handles all requests concurrently, so state must not be kept in fields.
The lifecycle is init once, service per request, destroy once; HttpServlet routes to doGet and doPost.
Sessions overcome HTTP's statelessness with cookies, URL rewriting or HttpSession; filters and listeners add cross-cutting behaviour.
JSP pages are translated into servlets; EL and JSTL keep Java out of the page; MVC separates controller servlet, model classes and JSP views.
Escaping output, prepared statements, HTTPS and careful session handling are the basic defences.

units.title: JavaBeans and the Enterprise Java Landscape
topics: Beans in JSP and in frameworks
Seeing the ideas: beans, events, serialization and the enterprise map

sections.title: Beans in JSP and in frameworks
Seeing the ideas: beans, events, serialization and the enterprise map

summary: A JavaBean is a serializable class with a no-argument constructor and private properties exposed through getters and setters; tools discover these by introspection.
Bound properties announce changes; constrained properties let listeners veto them before they take effect.
Beans connect the layers of an application (DAO, servlet, JSP, GUI) and are the basis of form binding in frameworks.
The enterprise Java stack (Jakarta EE, Spring) builds on the same ideas: servlets, JDBC, beans, injection and transactions.
